=== FINDING 1 (NEW, mine, CONFIRMED by probe, blocking) -- scripts/lwb_auto_queue.py accepts a review record that names NO commit, because `head.startswith("")` is True ===
scripts/lwb_auto_queue.py::review_records does:
    reviewed = str(record.get("reviewed_commit", ""))
    ...
    if not head.startswith(reviewed):
A missing or empty `reviewed_commit` becomes "", and every string starts with "". So a record with no `reviewed_commit` at all passes the freshness test and is counted as a satisfied independent review by the ARMED MERGE PATH.
REPRODUCTION (driving the PR's own FakeRepo harness from tests/test_lwb_auto_queue.py against the real aq.readiness; script at /tmp probe, not committed):
    A. unmutated good record                      -> ready=True   (harness sane)
    B. `reviewed_commit` key REMOVED              -> ready=True   <-- DEFECT
    C. `reviewed_commit` = ""                     -> ready=True   <-- DEFECT
    D. `reviewed_commit` = "a" (1-char prefix)    -> ready=True   <-- DEFECT
    E. `reviewed_commit` = "deadbeefdeadbeef"     -> ready=False, "reviewed_commit deadbeefdead is not this head"
E is the control: the probe is not vacuous, the check does refuse a genuinely wrong sha. B/C/D are the hole.
WHY IT MATTERS AND WHY IT IS THIS PR'S: scripts/lwb_auto_queue.py is NEW in this PR (422 lines, added by 88378a0). It re-implements the review gate independently of scripts/lwb_lanes.py, and the canonical gate guards exactly this case and this one does not -- lwb_lanes._review_ok has `or len(reviewed_commit) < 7 or not head_sha.startswith(reviewed_commit)`; lwb_auto_queue.review_records has only the startswith. reviews/README.md says in plain words why the binding exists: a record keyed to the PR rather than the commit "would have kept satisfying the gate and merged code it had never seen." A record naming no commit at all is that failure in its purest form, and the armed path is the one component whose decision actually merges.
This is also two of the three defect shapes this repository has named for itself: "reads one field of a config object and silently ignores a sibling field that changes the meaning", and "cannot distinguish 'I checked and found nothing' from 'I could not check'" -- here, "this record reviewed the head" and "this record does not say what it reviewed" have the identical representation.
FIX, one line, mirroring the canonical gate:
    if not isinstance(reviewed, str) or len(reviewed) < 7 or not head.startswith(reviewed):
and add a refusal test alongside the 27 already in tests/test_lwb_auto_queue.py; re-running probe B/C/D above must then print ready=False.

This is the finding the previous reviewer raised at ae29b1a. I did not take it on trust; I reproduced it at THIS head.
tests/test_lwb_auto_queue.py:411:
    unpinned = [s for s in steps if not (s.get("with") or {}).get("ref")]
Any non-empty `ref` satisfies it, including the pull request's own head. The assertion's failure text tells the reader to pin `ref: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}`, but the predicate never reads the value.
MY REPRODUCTION at 8a83970 (both files restored afterwards; `git status --short` empty, and tests/test_lwb_auto_queue.py re-run clean at 27 passed):
  1. Added to the REAL .github/workflows/lwb-auto-queue.yml, verbatim:
         pull_request:
           branches:
             - main
  2. Pinned the real checkout step to:
         - uses: actions/checkout@v7
           with:
             ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
  3. `python -m pytest tests/test_lwb_auto_queue.py -q` -> 27 passed in 0.06s
That is pull-request-controlled code executing in a job declaring `pull-requests: write`, and it is not a contrived shape: `github.event.pull_request.head.sha` is the ordinary way to check out PR code, so it is what the future edit this guard exists for would actually look like. By this repository's own stated standard -- a check that still passes when you break what it guards is vacuous -- the guard is still vacuous against the canonical hazard, narrower than the substring version it replaced but the same class.

=== FINDING 4 (NEW at this head, CONFIRMED, blocking the merge regardless of verdict) -- the branch now CONFLICTS with main, so no pull_request CI can run at all ===
Read live, not inferred:
  - `gh api repos/.../pulls/29` -> "mergeable": false, "mergeable_state": "dirty".
  - Locally, after `git fetch origin main`: `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only 8a83970 origin/main` reports `CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in HANDOFF.md`.
  - `gh api repos/.../actions/runs?branch=cloud/runbook` -> 13 runs. CI (event `pull_request`) exists for 74d0590a and 8d75890b ONLY, both `failure`. There is NO CI and NO Handoff run for 665d12e, dd9e1ad, 7b0d56e, 41c1690, ae29b1a or 8a83970 -- only the push-triggered lwb-auto-queue.
  - `gh api repos/.../commits/8a83970.../check-runs` -> exactly one run, "decide: completed/success" (lwb-auto-queue).
The previous reviewer reported the missing CI runs as finding E and said they could not determine the cause. I believe the cause is this: GitHub builds the `refs/pull/N/merge` commit that `pull_request` workflows check out, and when the merge is conflicted that ref cannot be produced, so the workflows do not run at all. The timing fits -- CI stops exactly at the point the branch and main diverge in HANDOFF.md. I state this as my best reading, not as something I measured directly: I cannot reproduce GitHub's internal ref construction, and the Actions settings endpoints are 403 through this proxy. What IS measured is the consequence, and it is not ambiguous: none of the nine contexts the ruleset requires has reported at this head, and the six `test (...)` legs have never reported success on this branch at any commit. "CI green" is not merely unproven here; it is currently unobtainable without updating the branch.

=== FINDING 6 (CONFIRMED, PRE-EXISTING on main, NOT charged to this PR, but decisive for what any reviewer can do here) ===
A stale DISAGREE record hard-fails `lwb-lanes` forever. In scripts/lwb_lanes.py::_review_ok the verdict test (line 646) runs BEFORE the staleness test (line 660) and APPENDS TO `errors` rather than merely declining to count the record. So reviews/29/cloud-reviewer.json (reviewed dd9e1ad, long superseded) and reviews/29/cloud-reviewer-2.json (reviewed ae29b1a, superseded) both fail the gate permanently, and this record will too. A stale AGREE at the same position would correctly be skipped as stale; only a stale DISAGREE is eternal.
    $ python scripts/lwb_lanes.py --base 9b374b5 --head 8a83970 --pr-number 29
    FAIL: reviews/29/cloud-reviewer-2.json: verdict is 'DISAGREE', want 'AGREE'   (x10, once per commit)
    exit status 1
`git diff origin/main HEAD -- scripts/lwb_lanes.py` adds only the two SHARED_PREFIXES entries, so this is main's defect, not this branch's, and it belongs in its own PR. I record it because it means the only mechanical route to a green lwb-lanes on PR #29 is to DELETE another reviewer's adverse record, which reviews/README.md itself calls falsifying evidence. The correct fix is in lwb_lanes.py: skip a record whose reviewed_commit is not the reviewable head BEFORE consulting its verdict, for every verdict alike.
FOR THE SAME REASON I did not write to reviews/29/cloud-reviewer.json, the filename my dispatching routine names: that file holds another reviewer's record and overwriting it would destroy evidence. reviews/README.md states the filename does not matter, so this record is reviews/29/cloud-reviewer-3.json. Deviation recorded here rather than resolved silently.
